items: 12 V pure sine wave inverter (or inverter/charger), 2,000–3,000 W, matched to the RV battery voltage
why: ChatGPT treated the question as one purchase: it recommended a single 2,000 W (or 3,000 W) pure sine inverter, showed individual inverter cards at $364.99, $414.99 and $949, and offered 'just an inverter' as the first path, so the panels-to-controller-to-battery diagram was background, not a required set. What decides the right pick is matching the inverter's DC input to the battery bank (12/24/48 V) and its wattage to the appliances. That is a choice between single models (and Dealectric's only listed inverters are 48 V split-phase home units that don't fit an RV), not a kit to assemble.
